subject: zoology_2
question_text: Name the ear ossicles and their evolutionary origin in human beings.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.50, VSAQ 79. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three ossicles
steps.why: The three small bones pass the vibration from the ear drum to the inner ear in a chain.
common_mistakes: Naming only two. There are three.
Naming the cochlea. That is not an ossicle.
steps.memory_tip: Hammer, anvil, stirrup — malleus, incus, stapes.
steps.margin_note: Just the three names here. Their origins come in the next line.
lines: The three ear ossicles are the malleus,

steps.label: Their origin
steps.why: The jaw bones of the reptile ancestor became the sound-carrying bones of the mammal ear.
common_mistakes: Mixing the pairs up. Malleus from articular, incus from quadrate.
steps.memory_tip: Articular becomes malleus, quadrate becomes incus, hyomandibular becomes stapes.

insider_note: Both halves are marked: the three names and the three origins. Name the three ossicles, then pair each one with the bone it came from.
